fed.lastMove: On September 16, 2026 the Fed raised its target rate by 0.25%, its first increase since 2023, because inflation has stayed above 3% all year.
fed.outlook: Most Fed officials expect one more increase by the end of 2026, then no change in 2027. Markets are pricing in another 0.25% increase in December.

forecasts.note: Based on rates as of August 31, before the September jump.
Expects rates to hold near 6.5% through 2027.

aboveForecastNote: Rates today are well above these forecasts, which were made before September's jump. Expect forecasters to raise them in their next updates.

scenarios.name: Fed keeps raising
scenarios.explanation: The Fed raises again in December and signals more. Mortgage rates tend to drift up when that's expected: about +0.35% over six months.

scenarios.name: Fed pauses after one more
scenarios.explanation: One more increase, then a long pause. Rates stay close to where they are today, easing slightly as the pause becomes clear.

scenarios.name: Inflation cools
scenarios.explanation: Inflation falls faster than expected and the Fed stops raising. Rates move back toward Fannie Mae's 6.7% forecast.
